step1_analysis.description: This circuit operates in the subthreshold region to compute a non-linear function (approximately squaring) of the input current. It is typically used in cochlear implants for envelope detection or RMS energy extraction of a full-wave rectified signal, amplifying nA-level currents to uA-level for subsequent processing.

paper_reference.title: A 126-W Cochlear Chip for a Totally Implantable System

power_consumption.description: Static power dissipation of the input mirroring branches at a nominal 10nA input current.

paper_reported.value: 80 nW (likely for a sub-block) / 126 uW (entire chip)

sky130_expected.calculation: The input current (10nA) is mirrored by the PMOS pair (XM1, XM2). Total current from VDD is approximately 2 * 10nA = 20nA. Power = 20nA * 1.8V = 36nW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Power is dominated by the subthreshold bias currents in the input mirror branches.

Iout_10nA.description: Output current (drain of XM5) when the input current is 10nA.

sky130_expected.calculation: At Iin = 10nA, XM3 and XM4 are deep in subthreshold. V_X = V_GS3 + V_GS4 ≈ 0.4V. XM5 operates near threshold, producing a current in the low microamp range.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The exponential dependence of Iout on V_X makes this highly sensitive to Vth and the subthreshold slope.

Iout_50nA.description: Output current (drain of XM5) when the input current is 50nA.

sky130_expected.calculation: As Iin increases to 50nA, V_X increases by ~2*n*Vt*ln(5) ≈ 100mV. V_X reaches ~0.5V to 0.6V, pushing XM5 into moderate/strong inversion. Iout ≈ 0.5 * beta * Vov^2 ≈ 30uA.
sky130_expected.reasoning: XM5 acts as a high-gain non-linear amplifier as it transitions from subthreshold to strong inversion, providing massive current gain.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure static power, DC non-linear transfer characteristics, and transient response to a rectified-like sine wave input.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Subthreshold Current Amplifier Testbench
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u

VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VLABEL_NET_0 LABEL_NET_0 0 0.9
VN1 N1 0 0

* Input current source pulling to GND (simulating rectified signal)
* DC value for OP/DC, SIN for Tran
Iin FULL_WAVE_RECTIFIED_SIGNAL 0 DC 10n SIN(50n 40n 1k)

XM5 LABEL_NET_0 VX N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM1 FULL_WAVE_RECTIFIED_SIGNAL FULL_WAVE_RECTIFIED_SIGNAL VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM3 VY VY N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM2 VX FULL_WAVE_RECTIFIED_SIGNAL VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM4 VX VX VY GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}

.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.control
  * 1. DC Operating Point
  op
  let pwr = -i(VVDD)*1.8
  print pwr

  * 2. DC Sweep for Transfer Characteristic
  dc Iin 1n 100n 1n
  let Iout_dc = -i(VLABEL_NET_0)
  meas dc Iout_10n find Iout_dc at=10n
  meas dc Iout_50n find Iout_dc at=50n

  * 3. Transient Analysis (Rectified-like sine wave)
  tran 10u 2m
  let Iout_tran = -i(VLABEL_NET_0)
  meas tran Iout_max max Iout_tran
  meas tran Iout_min min Iout_tran

  quit
.endc
.end
